main_body: A wooden pew drawn as a flat front view: horizontal plank bands (back rest and seat planks) stacked in a rectangle between two vertical side posts, with no visible seat surface from above.
top_band: none clear: rows 1-3 mid-brown (L~121) directly under a dark outline row 0, but it has the same tone family as the faces below; the lighter bands at rows 7 and 10 (L=157) are 1-row plank edges only
evidence: The column scan shows alternating dark and mid-brown 1-3 row bands, with only 1-row light lines at rows 7 and 10. No consistent lighter horizontal surface sits above a front face. The top rows 1-3 (L=121) are within 25 L of the plank faces below, so they belong to the front face. This reads as a flat front elevation of stacked planks with side posts. There is no seat surface seen from above, so it fails the seat requirement.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile for the references. The shading is limited to a few brown steps (dark, mid, light plank edge) and the surface is built from simple horizontal stripes with only faint grain marks on the planks. The outlines are tinted dark brown (17% neutral), which matches the Beodeul approach, and there are no large flat 5x5 fills. Overall it is clearly thinner and simpler than the reference stall and well.
